articles.content: Support our Journalism Depth, context and analysis Subscribe Home ANI Press Releases India’s First Agentic AI Campus Takes Shape at KLH Hyderabad ANI Press Releases India’s First Agentic AI Campus Takes Shape at KLH Hyderabad ANI PR 06 October, 2026 12:32 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin India’s First Agentic AI Campus Takes Shape at KLH Hyderabad Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ VMPL Hyderabad (Telangana) [India], October 6: KLH Hyderabad today inaugurated its Agentic AI Campus initiative and signed an MoU with HCL Group AI Labs, unveiling a roadmap that places AI-powered learning and student innovation at the centre of its academic vision. The collaboration aims to equip students across disciplines to understand, build and apply intelligent technologies through practical projects, faculty mentorship and industry engagement. Mr. Deepak Sarvanan, National Head, HCL Group AI Labs, formally inaugurated the initiative at a press meet in KLH Bachupally campus in Hyderabad. Show Full Article Dr. L. Koteswara Rao, Principal, KLH Bachupally, represented KLH at the MoU exchange, alongside Dr. A. Srinath, Dean – Skill Development, in the presence of other senior officials, deans, faculty and staff. The initiative aims to make AI an integral part of the student experience. From exploring concepts in the classroom to developing applications, students will be encouraged to use AI to investigate problems, test ideas and create solutions relevant to industry and society. Er. Koneru Lakshman Havish, Vice President, KL Deemed to be University said, “We want students to develop the confidence and skills to shape how AI is used in their chosen fields. Our collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs will help connect classroom learning with hands-on projects and industry expertise, giving students opportunities to build intelligent solutions for real-world needs. As we develop our Agentic AI Campus, our focus is on preparing young people to innovate responsibly and contribute meaningfully to an evolving workplace.” Agentic AI brings a new dimension to this approach. These systems can plan and carry out a series of tasks towards a defined goal, with appropriate human oversight. Understanding how such systems work will help students explore applications that extend from analysing information to coordinating workflows and supporting decisions. The proposed roadmap envisages project-based learning in areas such as business automation, data-driven services and discipline-specific AI applications. Students will be encouraged to design and test solutions, evaluating their accuracy, reliability and practical value. Faculty readiness will be a key part of the campus’s development. The collaboration envisages supporting educators in integrating AI into teaching, assignments and mentorship, helping students connect technical understanding with critical thinking and independent judgement. Responsible AI use will remain central to the learning approach, with attention to data privacy, bias, reliability and human accountability. Students will be encouraged to question outputs, verify information and understand the limitations of the systems they develop and use. articles.title: BULLET Microdrama to roll out 100+ AI titles powered by Trinetra AI - Adgully.com
articles.content: BULLET Microdrama, the platform backed by ZEE Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. (‘Z’), is expanding its content slate with the rollout of 100+ AI-powered microdramas , with Do Deewane aur Ashiqui as the first title to go live. The initiative brings together BULLET’s production partners and Trinetra AI - India’s first one of its kind AI-native filmmaking and content intelligence platform to build a larger pipeline of short-form, vertical and creator-driven stories for mobile-first audiences. The slate builds on BULLET’s focus on scaling the microdrama format while giving creators greater flexibility to experiment with new narratives, genres and story worlds. The story of Do Deewane Aashiqui follows Aditya, a young man who despises the wealthy after a powerful family causes his brother’s life to unravel. He falls for Ruhi, unaware that she is the daughter of the very businessman he holds responsible. As Ruhi hides her identity, their love grows, but when Aditya discovers the truth, he must choose between his love for her and his deep-rooted hatred for the world she comes from. To bring the wider slate of 100+ titles to audiences, BULLET Microdrama has partnered with multiple creative agencies like The Dosa Studios, The Filmy Musketeers Studio, FrameFry Studios, De Works Communications, SQB Pictures, Rajtaru Studio Limited and JVD Films. The partnership includes microdramas being developed end-to-end using BULLET’s Trinetra AI platform. The platform supports creators across multiple stages of the filmmaking process, from story development and visualisation to production. Trinetra AI’s script intelligence arm, Trishul, evaluates scripts across 100+ parameters to identify story strength and regional fit, while Rudra, the neural narrative generation engine supports storyboarding, character and universe creation, shot breakdown and video generation. Its audio orchestration model, Damrooh, takes care of dialect-accurate dialogues and background music. The slate also explores story worlds and genres that can be complex or expensive to execute through conventional production. Set against distinctive backdrops, including underwater and superhero universes, these titles demonstrate the creative range of AI-enabled production across different storytelling environments. For a format built around 60–100 high-hook episodes, AI enables greater production speed and scale while giving creators more room to experiment with stories, worlds and formats. It also expands the ecosystem to AI artists and creative talent beyond traditional production hubs, with BULLET positioning AI as a complement to, rather than a replacement for live-action production. Azim Lalani, Co-Founder & Chief Business Officer, BULLET Microdrama , said, “AI is beginning to change the economics of content, not simply by making production cheaper, but by changing how BULLET Microdrama decides where to place its bets. There is immense opportunity in building a tighter feedback loop between what is written, what is produced and what audiences actually respond to. For microdrama, where creators are constantly testing new narratives and formats, this marks a shift from learning afterwards to learning faster and making sharper choices. Over time, I believe this will change how content is developed, how portfolios are built, how IP is created and how value is generated in the...

articles.title: HSL Vizag Launches India's First Indigenous Fleet Support Ship
articles.content: Team Yo! Vizag Visakhapatnam , News/City Updates 3 hours ago Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Vizag, began as Scindia Shipyard in 1941, when industrialist Walchand Hirachand sought to build ships locally rather than rely on UK-built vessels. Dr Rajendra Prasad laid the foundation stone on June 21, 1941, and the shipyard’s landmark moment came on March 14, 1948, with the launch of SS Jala Usha, the first steamship built in the Indian subcontinent after World War II. In 85 years, HSL has progressed from producing a single steamship to indigenous warships, diving support vessels and Fleet Support Ships. Today, on 6 October 2026, the shipyard has entered a new chapter, as Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh made his maiden visit to mark three significant milestones: new capacity for ship-building, the launch of India’s first indigenous Fleet Support Ship, ‘Surya’, and a keel-laying for the next one. Over the past fifteen months, HSL has already been delivering one milestone after another. In July 2025, it commissioned INS Nistar, India’s first indigenously designed and built Diving Support Vessel, with over 80% indigenous content and capabilities not found in any previous naval Diving Support Vessel worldwide. On 30 August 2026, the second Diving Support Vessel, INS Nipun, joined the fleet, strengthening the Navy’s deep-sea diving and submarine rescue capability. The launch of three more breakthroughs today added to HSL’s proud achievements. These include an upgraded Slipway-4, supported by a 300-tonne Goliath Crane built under Make in India by M/s L&T Geostructure with Konecranes, which now enables the shipyard to build and launch ships of up to 45,000 DWT. FSS-1, named ‘Surya,’ the first of five Fleet Support Ships being built for the Indian Navy, is also entering the waters of the Bay of Bengal today, just 18 months after steel cutting. These 43,500-tonne vessels will replenish warships at sea, extending the Navy’s endurance and reach across the Indian Ocean Region. Lastly, the keel laying of FSS-5 then marked HSL’s steady march towards producing the rest of the ships in the series. Commenting on the latest developments, Rear Admiral C Raghuram, VSM (Retd.), Chairman & Managing Director, HSL, said, “Two warships commissioned, a record year and now three milestones in a single day. From our best-ever year to this historic day, every milestone reflects a shipyard rising to the nation’s call, and 6th October marks our next leap forward.” Speaking on the occasion, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said, “HSL is strengthening India’s maritime foundation as a national custodian of the country’s maritime capabilities. Together with the Naval Dockyard and the Port, it anchors Vizag’s maritime ecosystem, reflecting the expertise and engineering talent of our workforce. Fleet support will further advance our vision for the Indian Ocean, given its economic, energy and national security significance. From today, HSL must prepare for the Indian Navy’s requirements in the years ahead, while Vizag must prepare for the maritime industry India will need in the future.” Looking back at how far HSL has come, the contrast is striking. articles.title: Oolka, India's AI -Powered Credit Platform, Brings Credit Analysis, Dispute Management and ...
articles.content: PNN Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], October 6: Oolka, India’s AI-powered credit platform, brings credit analysis, dispute management and credit profile improvement together in a single app. The platform is now used by more than one crore Indians across 19,065 of the country’s roughly 19,100 pincodes, in all 36 states and union territories. For most borrowers, fixing a credit problem has meant working across several disconnected places. A score app shows the number. Disputes go through the credit bureau’s own process. NOCs and closure letters are chased separately with each lender. Conversations about settlement or restructuring happen over the phone, often with no written record. Oolka brings these steps into one place, and its AI credit assistant , Oolka AI, carries out much of the work itself. Credit analysis Oolka AI reads a user’s Experian credit report line by line and explains it in plain language, in more than 100 Indian languages. It identifies the specific entries weakening a user’s credit profile, such as repaid loans still showing as active, incorrect late-payment records, duplicate accounts and high credit card utilisation. Users do not need to know the terminology to ask. One in three Oolka users sends screenshots of financial documents and messages to have them explained, and 40 lakh messages have arrived as voice notes. Dispute management When Oolka AI finds an error, it acts on it. It files disputes and handles the follow-up communication with the credit bureau, drafts NOC and account-closure requests to lenders, and tracks each case until it is resolved. It keeps a record of every dispute, email and lender reply across the full history of a user’s case, so nobody has to start over or explain their situation twice. Credit profile improvement Beyond correcting errors, Oolka AI builds a personalised repayment plan that tackles the costliest debt first and reworks the order as loans close. It flags when card utilisation is too high, suggests consolidation where it lowers the total cost, and drafts restructuring, settlement and penalty-waiver requests to lenders. The improvements show up where lenders look first. More than 14,000 Oolka users now see their credit score rise in a typical week, three times the weekly figure in June. In one case, a school-van operator in Gurugram came to Oolka with a credit score that had stayed flat. Oolka AI traced the problem to his credit profile: a ₹5 overdue balance was keeping one account marked as active and overdue, holding back his entire file, and his card utilisation sat above 80%. Once the balance was cleared and his utilisation brought under control, his score began improving and he was approved for a consumer loan. “A credit score tells you something is wrong. It doesn’t tell you what’s wrong – or help you fix it. People came to Oolka not because they needed another credit score, but because they needed someone to read their report, find the problem, and get it resolved. articles.title: Pune To Host India's First Advanced Centre For Ergonomics And Human Factors Research
articles.content: Oct 06, 2026 | Updated 10:55 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and COEP Technological University will jointly set up the country's first Advanced Ergonomics and Human Factors Research Centre (AEHFRC) in Pune, with a planned investment of Rs 105 crore. The centre will come up at COEP Tech's Research and Innovation Park in Chikhali. It will develop engineering technologies and products built around the physical traits, needs and working conditions of Indian users. A Letter of Intent (LoI) was signed on 5 October in the presence of COEP Tech Vice-Chancellor Prof. Sunil Bhirud, ARAI Director Dr Reji Mathai and officials from both institutions. According to ARAI, the facility will span nearly 38,000 square feet. It aims to build domestic expertise in the field and reduce India's reliance on technologies largely designed for European users. In line with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision, it will serve as a dedicated hub for research, testing, validation, training and innovation. The project will be executed in two phases. The first, spanning two to three years, will set up or upgrade facilities for posture evaluation, seating comfort analysis, human biomechanics and field-of-vision assessment. Over the following four to five years, the second phase will develop the AEHFRC into a full-fledged National Centre of Excellence. The centre will serve sectors including automotive, defence, aerospace, railways, agriculture, industrial equipment, consumer goods, furniture, construction and textiles. It will help industries assess how their products and systems interact with users in order to improve safety, efficiency and comfort. Its testing and validation support is expected to help companies address aspects such as vehicle seating, driver posture, visibility, workplace design and human-machine interaction early in product development. The centre will also offer specialised training and certification programmes. By linking academic research with industry needs, it aims to turn scientific findings into practical applications. articles.title: Airtel Business Unveils IQ Gateway: India's First Telco-Grade Enterprise Messaging Platform
articles.content: Airtel Business today launched Airtel IQ Gateway, India’s first ever telco-grade network intelligence platform which brings different customer communication channels onto one safe control plane. Enterprises now won’t need to manage multiple vendors separately if they opt for Airtel IQ Gateway, a DPDP-compliant platform which combines SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, voice communications and number verification (silent authentication) together in one place. It will enable enterprises to easily manage their business communications at scale, while protecting customer trust and making safety foundational to every customer interaction. This offering from Airtel Business is of critical importance today, when businesses have to manage fragmented customer communication stacks across multiple service providers and tools to reach their customers, with limited visibility into the real delivery of messages. Messages are often reported delivered even when they fail, while International OTP pumping by bots inflates bills. Moreover, managing pre-approved message templates is manual and often leads to mistakes. For enterprises, especially in sectors like BFSI, government, e‑commerce and logistics, this not only hurts customer trust when consumers are targeted by scams, this also damages their brand reputation. Airtel IQ Gateway solves this with a single control center for all business communications. It brings together Airtel’s fraud protection with automatic integrations of native message template system (DLT), automatic switching to back-up service providers, and intelligent routing across SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice. By leveraging Airtel’s built-in network intelligence and trust layers for enterprise use, such as IQ Verify for fraud protection and Silent Authentication for SIM based login, with capabilities like spotting fraudulent account creations and takeovers and artificial traffic spikes, Airtel IQ Gateway protects enterprises from fraud losses and billing spikes caused by industry-wide SMS pumping. Launched nationwide today after successful trial deployments across select banks, financial institutions and other relevant industry collaborations, the platform extends Airtel’s proven expertise in fraud prevention for end customers to enterprises, enabling them to build customer trust at scale through safe communications. Sharat Sinha, CEO – Airtel Business, said, “As India accelerates towards a safe, inclusive digital economy, trust must become the foundation of every digital interaction. Secure-by-design customer engagement is today the bedrock on which enterprises can scale with confidence. At Airtel, we have already demonstrated the power of network-grade fraud prevention in protecting millions of consumers across our mobile and digital services. With IQ Gateway, we are extending this proven expertise to enterprises, enabling them to build brand trust while ensuring every customer conversation is safe, authenticated and resilient. By embedding trust at the network layer, we are enabling our enterprise customers, especially banks, government departments and logistics firms, to reduce cybercrime losses and strengthen the credibility of every customer interaction. This is a decisive step towards a safer digital future for India, where citizens and businesses can transact and engage with equal confidence.” Key capabilities of Airtel IQ Gateway Flexible deployment: It can be integrated with existing communication workflows and vendor ecosystems.
